channel.title: AI Campaign News (AICN)
channel.description: A tracker of AI use in political campaigns, elections, and advocacy.

item.title: We've tracked $80M of spending on almost 170 AI-generated political ads this year – it's weird
item.description: An ad-tracking effort has identified roughly 170 AI-generated political ads with approximately $80 million in combined spending in 2026, finding that many of these ads carry no AI disclosure due to inconsistent state-level requirements.

item.title: How AI is playing in the post-Nancy Pelosi race
item.description: In the California congressional race to succeed Nancy Pelosi, campaigns for state Sen. Scott Wiener and San Francisco Supervisor Connie Chan have both deployed paid ads explicitly invoking artificial intelligence, making AI a central message in the contest.

item.title: OpenAI wants to curb misleading election deepfakes
item.description: OpenAI is taking steps to make it harder for users to generate misleading election deepfakes through its platforms, implementing restrictions targeting bad actors seeking to interfere in U.S. elections.

item.title: Voters Aren’t Comfortable With the Most Public-Facing Uses of AI In Politics, Poll Finds
item.description: A new national survey commissioned by the AAPC Foundation finds that voters are uncomfortable with the most public-facing uses of AI in political campaigns, providing some of the clearest polling data yet on public attitudes toward campaigns' growing AI adoption.

item.title: Bilingual AI app helps Latinos figure out how to vote
item.description: A bilingual AI app called Nubi is being used to help Latino voters navigate the voting process ahead of the 2026 midterms, serving as a voter-outreach and civic-guidance tool targeting a key demographic.

item.title: Political Campaign Use of AI-Powered Voter Outreach Highlights Regulatory Gaps
item.description: The Center for Democracy and Technology published an analysis examining how political campaigns are using AI-powered voter outreach tools and the regulatory gaps that current frameworks leave unaddressed.

item.title: Campaigning for the AI ‘vote’
item.description: Campaign Trend's newsletter roundup covers Inbox.GOP's latest spam data on AI-generated political email and recent deepfake-related lawsuits in the political arena.

item.title: Good Intentions Are Not Safeguards: Katie Harbath on What Social Media Should Teach Us About AI
item.description: Katie Harbath, a veteran of Facebook's policy work, argues that the campaign and political ecosystem cannot simply replicate the social media governance playbook for AI and must apply lessons learned to build new safeguards proactively.

item.title: Van Orden Hit With Cease-and-Desist Letter Over AI Deepfake Videos
item.description: Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent Rep. Derrick Van Orden's campaign a cease-and-desist letter, alleging the Wisconsin Republican's campaign used AI-generated deepfake videos to falsely attribute statements to Cooke.

item.title: Q&A: How Big Tech Forever Changed the Campaign World
item.description: Campaigns & Elections features a Q&A with Katie Harbath, a longtime tech-politics veteran, who reflects on how campaigns misjudged social media's early potential and what the AI era now means for political campaigning.

item.title: L2 and IVC Media Launch Voter Count, an AI Agent That Answers Plain-English Questions About the National Voter File
item.description: L2 and IVC Media have launched VoterCount.ai, a conversational AI agent that lets users ask plain-English questions directly against L2's national voter file of more than 217 million registered voters and receive answers in seconds. The companies describe it as the only AI tool with a direct live connection to a national voter file.

item.title: Can AI Produce the Most Informed Electorate in History?
item.description: A Campaign Trend piece argues that AI is narrowing the information gap between political insiders and ordinary voters at the local level, and that campaigns will increasingly face constituents who arrive at conversations already informed — changing how voter outreach must be designed.

item.title: Synthetic Respondents Need a Label Before They Need a Benchmark
item.description: A Victorino Group commentary argues that the most pressing problem with synthetic survey respondents is not accuracy benchmarking but the absence of mandatory labeling — research buyers currently cannot tell whether data they purchase includes AI-simulated responses, even as vendors in the space carry billion-dollar valuations while subgroup accuracy remains weak.

item.title: AI Is Changing What Campaigns Should Expect From Voter Outreach
item.description: A Campaigns & Elections practitioner piece argues that AI's primary value in voter outreach is not generating more content but expanding a campaign's capacity to respond quickly and at scale to voter contact.

item.title: New campaign disclosures reveal how much American political campaigns spend on AI tools
item.description: An analysis drawing on FEC campaign-finance disclosures examines how much U.S. political campaigns are spending on AI tools, providing empirical data on actual AI adoption and expenditure across campaigns.

item.title: AI Data Centers Emerge as a Hot Topic for Political Ads in 2026
item.description: An analysis by the Absecon Group found that more than 700 candidates in 2026 have run digital ads about AI data centers, establishing the issue as a significant campaign messaging theme this cycle.

item.title: AI ads are popular in the 2026 midterms, but state laws haven't stopped a lack of disclosure
item.description: The Washington Post reports that AI-generated ads are prevalent across the 2026 midterm campaigns but that state disclosure laws have largely not stopped campaigns from failing to label AI-generated content.

item.title: Google Pulled Down a Trump-Linked Ad That Used AI
item.description: Google removed an AI-generated political ad tied to a Trump-aligned PAC targeting a Texas race, citing the platform's requirement that political ads disclose AI-generated content.

item.title: Candidates embrace AI for political ads despite growing voter anxiety
item.description: The Hill reports that candidates across the political spectrum are increasingly using AI to produce political ads ahead of the 2026 midterms, even as polling shows growing voter unease about the practice.

item.title: Can AI Help Campaigns Reach Latino Voters?
item.description: Democratic creative firm Conexión is partnering with ad platform Mundial Media to offer campaigns AI-powered tools specifically designed to improve outreach and engagement with Latino voters.

item.title: Democratic campaigns, organizers urge to snub AI super PAC funds
item.description: Democratic campaigns and organizers sent a letter urging candidates to reject donations from AI-aligned super PACs, specifically calling out the group Leading Future, amid concerns about the political influence of AI industry money in the 2026 midterms.

item.title: Trump pollster Fabrizio gives Republican candidates advice on how to talk about AI data centers
item.description: Trump pollster Tony Fabrizio circulated messaging guidance to Republican candidates advising them on how to frame AI data centers as a campaign issue ahead of the 2026 midterms.

item.title: 2026 midterm elections: Helping voters navigate election information in the age of AI
item.description: Microsoft published a blog post describing its efforts to help voters identify reliable election information and understand AI-generated content ahead of the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, framing the initiative as a voter-navigation resource.

item.title: AI PACs Have Dumped Nearly $1 Million Into an Obscure Senate Race
item.description: PACs affiliated with AI companies and investors have spent close to $1 million in South Dakota's reliably Republican Senate race — outspending contributions from actual state residents — as AI-aligned political money flows into the 2026 midterms.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence PACs are growing in number
item.description: Punchbowl News reports that the number of AI-focused political action committees is growing rapidly ahead of the 2026 midterms and provides a rundown of AI-related groups currently spending money in campaigns.

item.title: AI reshaping political campaigns as SC weighs whether new rules are needed
item.description: A South Carolina local news report describes how campaigns are using AI to produce content faster and at lower cost, while state lawmakers consider whether new disclosure rules are needed.

item.title: As campaign season gears up, AI-generated ads are everywhere
item.description: NPR reports that as the 2026 midterm campaign season accelerates, AI-generated political ads have become ubiquitous, with campaigns across the country deploying synthetic media content at scale.

item.title: Human-Made Ads Still Perform Better Than AI Spots, Study Finds
item.description: A study covered by Campaigns & Elections found that consumers consistently prefer human-made political ads over AI-generated ones, with human-produced spots outperforming AI spots on key preference metrics.

item.title: AI-Generated Campaign Ads Are Eroding Trust in US Elections
item.description: A Bloomberg opinion piece argues that AI-generated campaign ads are undermining voter trust in U.S. elections and calls for stronger regulatory safeguards around their use.

item.title: KEN PAXTON BS AI Campaign Ad Features a Fake James Talarico Misquoting Himself
item.description: Ken Paxton's campaign released an AI-generated ad that depicts his opponent James Talarico appearing to misquote himself, fabricating a statement Talarico never made.
